verses.en: These things his disciples did not understand at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about him and that they had done these things to him.
So the crowd that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead was bearing witness.
For this reason also the crowd went to meet him, because they heard that he had done this sign.
So the Pharisees said to one another, “You see that you are gaining nothing. Look, the world has gone after him.”
Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
So these came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and were asking him, saying, “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.”
Philip comes and tells Andrew; Andrew and Philip come and tell Jesus.
And Jesus answers them, saying, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Truly, truly, I say to you, unless the grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
The one who loves his life loses it, and the one who hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me, and where I am, there my servant will be also; if anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.
Now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this reason I came to this hour.

cmp.w: pater, sōson me ek tēs hōras tautēs
cmp.note: 这一句照底本的标点是一句祷告；也可以读成问句：「我该说什么呢？说『父啊，救我脱离这个时刻』吗？」
cmp.en: As punctuated in this edition the sentence is a prayer; it can also be read as a question: "What shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this hour’?"

verses.en: Father, glorify your name.” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have both glorified it and will glorify it again.”
So the crowd that stood by and heard it was saying that it had thundered; others were saying, “An angel has spoken to him.”
Jesus answered and said, “This voice has not come for my sake but for yours.
Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out;
and I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”
Now he was saying this to signify by what kind of death he was going to die.
So the crowd answered him, “We have heard from the law that the Christ remains forever; and how do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”

So Jesus said to them, “For a little while longer the light is among you. Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you; and the one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become sons of light.” Jesus said these things, and going away he was hidden from them.
But though he had done so many signs before them, they were not believing in him,
so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: “Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

cmp.note: 引自旧约《以赛亚书》53:1。
cmp.en: Quoted from Isaiah 53:1.

verses.en: For this reason they could not believe, because again Isaiah said,
“He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, lest they see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them.”
Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory, and he spoke about him.
Nevertheless, many even of the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they were not confessing it, lest they be put out of the synagogue;
for they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.
And Jesus cried out and said, “The one who believes in me believes not in me but in him who sent me,
and the one who sees me sees him who sent me.
I have come as light into the world, that everyone who believes in me may not remain in the darkness.
And if anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world.
The one who rejects me and does not receive my words has one who judges him; the word that I spoke, that will judge him on the last day;
for I did not speak of myself, but the Father who sent me has himself given me a command, what to say and what to speak.
And I know that his command is eternal life. So the things I speak, just as the Father has told me, so I speak.”

chapters.title: Chapter 13 · Washing the Disciples’ Feet; Judas Leaves; the New Command
chapters.intro: At supper before the Passover, Jesus gets up and washes his disciples’ feet, telling them he has given them an example. He says that one of them will hand him over and gives a morsel of bread to Judas, who goes out; it is night. Jesus gives the disciples a new command, to love one another, and tells Peter that before a rooster crows he will deny him three times.

verses.en: Now before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour had come to depart out of this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end.
And during supper, the devil having already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to hand him over,
knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God,
he rises from supper and lays aside his garments, and taking a towel he tied it around himself.
Then he pours water into the basin and began to wash the feet of the disciples and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.
So he comes to Simon Peter. He says to him, “Lord, do you wash my feet?”
Jesus answered and said to him, “What I am doing you do not know now, but you will understand after these things.”
Peter says to him, “You shall never wash my feet.” Jesus answered him, “If I do not wash you, you have no part with me.”
Simon Peter says to him, “Lord, not my feet only but also my hands and my head.”
Jesus says to him, “The one who has bathed has no need except to wash his feet, but is clean all over; and you are clean, but not all of you.”
For he knew the one who was handing him over; for this reason he said, “Not all of you are clean.”
So when he had washed their feet and taken his garments and reclined again, he said to them, “Do you understand what I have done to you?
You call me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and you say well, for I am.
If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet;
for I gave you an example, that you also should do just as I did to you.
Truly, truly, I say to you, a slave is not greater than his master, nor is one who is sent greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
I am not speaking of all of you; I know whom I chose. But it is so that the scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one who eats my bread has lifted up his heel against me.’

cmp.w: epēren epʼ eme tēn pternan autou
cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》41:9。
cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 41:9.

verses.en: From now on I am telling you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am.
Truly, truly, I say to you, the one who receives whomever I send receives me, and the one who receives me receives him who sent me.”
Having said these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit and testified and said, “Truly, truly, I say to you, one of you will hand me over.”
The disciples were looking at one another, at a loss as to whom he was speaking of.
One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was reclining at table close to the chest of Jesus;
so Simon Peter nods to this one to ask who it might be of whom he is speaking.
That one, leaning back thus on the chest of Jesus, says to him, “Lord, who is it?”
Jesus answers, “It is that one for whom I will dip the morsel and give it to him.” So having dipped the morsel, he gives it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.
And after the morsel, then Satan entered into that one. So Jesus says to him, “What you are doing, do quickly.”
Now no one of those reclining at table knew for what purpose he said this to him;
for some were supposing, since Judas had the money box, that Jesus was saying to him, “Buy what we need for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.
So having taken the morsel, that one went out immediately. And it was night.
So when he had gone out, Jesus says, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him;
if God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him immediately.
Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You will seek me, and just as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come,’ so now I say to you also.
A new command I give to you, that you love one another; just as I loved you, that you also love one another.
By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”
Simon Peter says to him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered, “Where I am going you cannot follow me now, but you will follow later.”
Peter says to him, “Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”
Jesus answers, “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I say to you, a rooster will certainly not crow until you have denied me three times.”

chapters.title: Chapter 14 · The Way, the Truth, and the Life; the Helper Promised
chapters.intro: After supper Jesus speaks to his disciples, in a discourse that runs on to chapter 16. He tells them not to be troubled: he is going to prepare a place for them and will come again. Thomas, Philip and Judas each ask a question, and he answers, “I am the way and the truth and the life”; whoever has seen him has seen the Father. He promises to ask the Father to send another Helper, the Holy Spirit, and leaves them his peace.

verses.en: “Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me.

cmp.note: 两个「信」原文写法一样，前一个可以读成陈述（「你们信上帝」），也可以读成命令（「你们要信上帝」）。白话、英文与和合本都取前一种。
cmp.en: The two verbs for "believe" are spelled alike; the first can be a statement ("you believe in God") or a command ("believe in God"). All three versions here take it as a statement.

verses.en: In my Father’s house are many dwelling places; if it were not so, I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you;
and if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again and will take you to myself, so that where I am you may be also.
And where I am going, you know the way.”
Thomas says to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?”
Jesus says to him, “I am the way and the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except through me.
If you had known me, you would have known my Father also; from now on you know him and have seen him.”
Philip says to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.”
Jesus says to him, “Have I been with you so long a time, and you have not come to know me, Philip? The one who has seen me has seen the Father; how do you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I say to you I do not speak of myself, but the Father dwelling in me does his works.
Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father in me; or else believe because of the works themselves.
Truly, truly, I say to you, the one who believes in me, the works that I do he also will do, and greater than these he will do, because I am going to the Father;
and whatever you ask in my name, this I will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son;
if you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.
If you love me, you will keep my commands;
and I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper, to be with you forever,
the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him; you know him, because he remains with you and will be in you.
I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.
Yet a little while and the world no longer sees me, but you see me; because I live, you also will live.
In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
The one who has my commands and keeps them, that is the one who loves me; and the one who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will show myself to him.”
Judas, not Iscariot, says to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are going to show yourself to us and not to the world?”
Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him.
The one who does not love me does not keep my words; and the word that you hear is not mine but the Father’s who sent me.
These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you;
but the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and remind you of all that I said to you.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid.
You heard that I said to you, ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
I will no longer speak much with you, for the ruler of the world is coming; and in me he has nothing,
but so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father commanded me, so I do. Rise, let us go from here.”

chapters.title: Chapter 15 · The Vine and the Branches; the World’s Hatred
chapters.intro: From first verse to last this chapter is Jesus speaking, and the speech runs on into the next. He calls himself the vine and the disciples the branches: only by remaining in him can they bear fruit. His command is that they love one another, and he calls them friends, no longer slaves. He adds that the world, which has hated him, will hate them too; when the Helper comes he will bear witness about him, and they also are to bear witness.

verses.en: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser.
Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he takes away, and every one that bears fruit he prunes, that it may bear more fruit.

cmp.note: 「剪掉」和「修剪干净」在原文是读音相近的两个词；「修剪干净」和下一节的「干净」又是同一个词根。
cmp.en: In Greek "takes away" and "prunes" are two similar-sounding words, and "prunes" shares its root with "clean" in the next verse.

verses.en: Already you are clean because of the word that I have spoken to you.
Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit of itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in me.
I am the vine; you are the branches. The one who remains in me and I in him, this one bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
If anyone does not remain in me, he is thrown out like the branch and withers, and they gather them and throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.
Just as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you; remain in my love.
If you keep my commands, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commands and remain in his love.
These things I have spoken to you so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be made full.
This is my command, that you love one another just as I loved you.
Greater love than this no one has, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do what I command you.
No longer do I call you slaves, for the slave does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, for all that I heard from my Father I have made known to you.
You did not choose me, but I chose you, and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit and that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you.
These things I command you, that you love one another.
If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before you.
If you were of the world, the world would love its own; but because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A slave is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.
But all these things they will do to you on account of my name, because they do not know him who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
The one who hates me hates my Father also.
If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.
But it is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’

cmp.note: 这句话见于旧约《诗篇》35:19 和 69:4。《诗篇》不在摩西的律法书里，这里的「律法」是泛指整部经书。
cmp.en: The words are found in Psalms 35:19 and 69:4. The Psalms are not part of the law of Moses; "law" here stands for the scriptures as a whole.

verses.en: When the Helper comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness about me;
and you also bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.

chapters.title: Chapter 16 · The Helper Will Come; Sorrow Turned to Joy
chapters.intro: The chapter opens in mid-speech: Jesus is still talking to his disciples, as in the chapter before. They will be put out of the synagogue and even killed; he is going away, but only if he goes will the Helper come to guide them. He says that in "a little while" they will not see him and then will see him again, and the disciples cannot follow; he compares it to a woman in labor whose sorrow turns to joy. He ends by saying that he has overcome the world.

verses.en: These things I have spoken to you so that you may not be made to stumble.
They will put you out of the synagogue; indeed an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think he is offering service to God.
And they will do these things because they have not known the Father or me.
But these things I have spoken to you so that when their hour comes you may remember that I told you of them. And I did not say these things to you from the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
But I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away; for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment:
concerning sin, because they do not believe in me;
concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you see me no longer;
concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.

But when he comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you in all the truth; for he will not speak on his own, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things that are coming.
He will glorify me, because he will take from what is mine and declare it to you.
All that the Father has is mine; that is why I said that he takes from what is mine and will declare it to you.
A little while, and you see me no longer; and again a little while, and you will see me.”

So some of his disciples said to one another, “What is this that he says to us, ‘A little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me’; and, ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”
So they were saying, “What is this that he says, ‘a little while’? We do not know what he is talking about.”

Jesus knew that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, “Are you asking one another about this, that I said, ‘A little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me’?
Truly, truly, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.

A woman, when she is giving birth, has sorrow, because her hour has come; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the anguish, for joy that a human being has been born into the world.
So you also have sorrow now; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy away from you.
And in that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father, he will give it to you in my name.
Until now you have asked nothing in my name; ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be made full.
These things I have spoken to you in figures of speech; an hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech but will tell you plainly about the Father.

cmp.note: 原文 paroimia 指不直说的话、拐着弯的说法。另外三卷福音书里译作「比喻」的是另一个词 parabolē（打比方的故事），这卷书里没有用过那个词。和合本两个词都译「比喻」。
cmp.en: Greek paroimia means veiled or indirect speech. The word translated "parable" in the other three Gospels is a different one, parabolē, which this Gospel never uses. The Union Version renders both as 比喻 (bǐyù, "comparison, parable").

verses.en: In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf;
for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came out from God.
I came out from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and going to the Father.”
His disciples say, “Look, now you are speaking plainly and using no figure of speech.
Now we know that you know all things and have no need for anyone to question you; by this we believe that you came out from God.”
Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?
Look, an hour is coming, and has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and will leave me alone; and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
These things I have spoken to you so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have affliction; but take courage: I have overcome the world.”

chapters.title: Chapter 17 · Jesus Prays to the Father
chapters.intro: The whole chapter is Jesus praying to the Father. He says the hour has come and asks the Father to glorify him; he has finished the work the Father gave him and has passed the Father’s words on to those the Father gave him. He asks the Father to keep them, to make them holy and to make them one, and he prays also for those who will come to believe through their word. In the prayer "you" is God and "they" are the disciples.

verses.en: Jesus spoke these things, and lifting up his eyes to heaven he said, “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, so that the Son may glorify you,
just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that to all whom you have given him he may give eternal life.
And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.
I glorified you on the earth, having completed the work that you gave me to do;
and now, Father, glorify me in your own presence with the glory that I had with you before the world existed.
I made your name known to the people whom you gave me out of the world. They were yours and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now they know that everything you have given me is from you;
for the words that you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and came to know truly that I came out from you, and they believed that you sent me.
I ask on their behalf; I am not asking on behalf of the world but on behalf of those whom you have given me, because they are yours,
and all that is mine is yours, and yours is mine, and I have been glorified in them.
And I am no longer in the world, and they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, which you have given me, so that they may be one just as we are.
While I was with them, I kept them in your name, which you have given me, and I guarded them, and not one of them was lost except the son of destruction, so that the scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have my joy made full in themselves.
I have given them your word, and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil one.

cmp.note: 原文可以读成「那恶者」（指魔鬼），也可以读成「恶」（坏事）。白话和和合本都取前一种，和《马太福音》6:13 的写法一致。
cmp.en: The Greek can be read as "the evil one" (the devil) or as "evil" in general. The plain Chinese and the Union Version both take the first, as at Matthew 6:13.

verses.en: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.
Just as you sent me into the world, I also sent them into the world;
and for their sake I sanctify myself, so that they also may be sanctified in truth.
I do not ask on behalf of these only, but also on behalf of those who believe in me through their word,
that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.
The glory that you have given me I have given to them, so that they may be one just as we are one,
I in them and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me.
Father, I desire that those whom you have given me may be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you have given me because you loved me before the foundation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and these have known that you sent me;
and I made your name known to them, and will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

chapters.title: Chapter 18 · The Arrest, Annas, Peter’s Denials, Before Pilate
chapters.intro: Jesus and his disciples go to a garden across the Kidron, and Judas arrives with soldiers and officers to arrest him; Peter draws a sword and strikes, and Jesus stops him. Jesus is taken first to Annas and questioned, while in the courtyard Peter says three times that he is not one of his disciples. Early in the morning he is brought to the Roman governor Pilate, who asks whether he is a king and says he finds no case against him; but the crowd outside asks for the robber Barabbas to be released instead.

verses.en: Having said these things, Jesus went out with his disciples across the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, which he and his disciples entered.
Now Judas, who was handing him over, also knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with his disciples.
So Judas, having taken the cohort and officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.

cmp.note: 原文 speira 是罗马军队的一个营，满编约六百人；这里指一队罗马兵，人数经文没有说。和合本译「一队兵」，白话照此。
cmp.en: Greek speira is a Roman cohort, about six hundred men at full strength; here it means a detachment of Roman soldiers, and the text gives no number. The Union Version has 一队兵 (yí duì bīng, "a squad of soldiers"), which the plain Chinese follows.

verses.en: So Jesus, knowing all the things that were coming upon him, went out and says to them, “Whom are you seeking?”
They answered him, “Jesus the Nazarene.” He says to them, “I am.” And Judas, who was handing him over, was also standing with them.

cmp.note: 原文只有「我是」两个字，可以就是平常说的「是我」。同样两个字的说法在这卷书里出现过好几次（8:24、8:28、8:58、13:19）。
cmp.en: The Greek is just two words, "I am," which can simply mean "It is I." The same two-word phrase occurs several times earlier in this Gospel (8:24, 8:28, 8:58; 13:19).

verses.en: So when he said to them, “I am,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
So he asked them again, “Whom are you seeking?” And they said, “Jesus the Nazarene.”
Jesus answered, “I told you that I am; so if you are seeking me, let these men go.”
This was so that the word he had spoken might be fulfilled: “Of those whom you have given me I have lost not one.”
So Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his right ear. And the slave’s name was Malchus.
So Jesus said to Peter, “Put the sword into its sheath; the cup that the Father has given me, shall I not drink it?”
So the cohort and the commander and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him
and led him first to Annas; for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
Now Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it was expedient for one man to die for the people.
Now Simon Peter was following Jesus, and so was another disciple. And that disciple was known to the high priest, and he went with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest,
but Peter was standing at the door outside. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.
So the servant girl who kept the door says to Peter, “You are not also one of this man’s disciples, are you?” He says, “I am not.”
Now the slaves and the officers were standing there, having made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves; and Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.
So the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
Jesus answered him, “I have spoken openly to the world; I always taught in a synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews come together, and I spoke nothing in secret.
Why do you question me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them; look, these know what I said.”
And when he had said these things, one of the officers standing by gave Jesus a slap, saying, “Is that how you answer the high priest?”
Jesus answered him, “If I spoke wrongly, testify about the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike me?”
So Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. So they said to him, “You are not also one of his disciples, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
One of the slaves of the high priest, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, says, “Did I not see you in the garden with him?”
So Peter denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.
So they lead Jesus from Caiaphas to the praetorium. Now it was early morning. And they themselves did not enter the praetorium, so that they would not be defiled but might eat the Passover.
So Pilate went outside to them and says, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
They answered and said to him, “If this man were not doing evil, we would not have handed him over to you.”
So Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.” The Jews said to him, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death.”
This was so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which he spoke, signifying by what kind of death he was going to die.
So Pilate entered the praetorium again and called Jesus and said to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answered, “Do you say this of yourself, or did others tell you about me?”
Pilate answered, “Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me; what did you do?”

Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world; if my kingdom were of this world, my servants would be fighting, so that I would not be handed over to the Jews; but as it is, my kingdom is not from here.”

So Pilate said to him, “So you are a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I have come into the world, to testify to the truth; everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.”

cmp.note: 和另外三卷福音书里的「这是你说的」一样，这句话既不是直接承认，也不是否认。
cmp.en: Like "You say so" in the other three Gospels, this is neither a plain yes nor a denial.

verses.en: Pilate says to him, “What is truth?” And having said this, he went out again to the Jews and says to them, “I find no ground for a charge against him.
But you have a custom that I release one man to you at the Passover; so do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
So they cried out again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.

chapters.title: Chapter 19 · The Sentence, the Crucifixion, the Burial
chapters.intro: Pilate has Jesus flogged, and the soldiers mock him with a crown of thorns. Pilate says more than once that he finds no case against him and tries to release him, but the cry outside is for crucifixion, and Pilate hands him over. Jesus is crucified at Golgotha; he entrusts his mother to the disciple whom he loved, says "It is finished," and dies. Joseph and Nicodemus bury him in a new tomb in a garden.

verses.en: So then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.
And the soldiers, having woven a crown out of thorns, put it on his head, and threw a purple robe around him,
and they kept coming up to him and saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they gave him slaps.
And Pilate went outside again and says to them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I find no ground for a charge against him.”
So Jesus came outside, wearing the thorn crown and the purple robe. And he says to them, “Behold, the man!”

So when the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, saying, “Crucify, crucify!” Pilate says to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no ground for a charge against him.”
The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.”
So when Pilate heard this word, he was more afraid,
and he entered the praetorium again and says to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.
So Pilate says to him, “Do you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you and I have authority to crucify you?”
Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given to you from above; therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”
From then on Pilate was seeking to release him; but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you are not a friend of Caesar; everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.”
So when Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
Now it was the day of Preparation of the Passover; it was about the sixth hour. And he says to the Jews, “Behold, your King!”
So they cried out, “Away with him, away with him, crucify him!” Pilate says to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”
So then he handed him over to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus;
and carrying the cross by himself, he went out to what is called the Place of a Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha,
where they crucified him, and with him two others, one on either side, and Jesus in the middle.
And Pilate also wrote a notice and put it on the cross; and it was written, “Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews.”
So many of the Jews read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, in Greek.
So the chief priests of the Jews were saying to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but that he said, ‘I am King of the Jews.’”
Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
So the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier, and also the tunic. Now the tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout;

so they said to one another, “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, to see whose it will be.” This was so that the scripture might be fulfilled which says, “They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots.” So the soldiers did these things.

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《诗篇》22:18。那里两句是同一个意思说两遍；这里把它读成两件事：外面的衣服分了，里衣抽签。
cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 22:18. There the two lines say the same thing twice; here they are read as two acts: the outer garments divided, the tunic gambled for.

verses.en: Now there were standing by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

cmp.note: 原文只写「革罗罢的马利亚」，「妻子」是照通行的理解补的。「他母亲的姐妹」和「革罗罢的马利亚」中间没有连词，可以是两个人（一共四位妇女），也可以是同一个人（一共三位）。
cmp.en: The Greek says only "Mary of Clopas"; "wife" is supplied on the usual understanding. There is no conjunction between "his mother’s sister" and "Mary of Clopas," so they may be two women (four in all) or the same woman (three in all).

verses.en: So Jesus, seeing his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing by, says to his mother, “Woman, behold, your son.”
Then he says to the disciple, “Behold, your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
After this, Jesus, knowing that all things had now been finished, so that the scripture might be fulfilled, says, “I thirst.”
A jar full of sour wine was standing there; so they put a sponge full of the sour wine on a hyssop branch and brought it to his mouth.
So when Jesus had received the sour wine, he said, “It is finished,” and bowing his head, he gave up his spirit.

So the Jews, since it was the day of Preparation, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath, for that Sabbath was a great day, asked Pilate that their legs be broken and that they be taken away.
So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who had been crucified with him;
but coming to Jesus, when they saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs,
but one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
And the one who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true, and he knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
For these things happened so that the scripture might be fulfilled: “Not a bone of him shall be broken.”

cmp.note: 一般认为引的是旧约里关于逾越节羊羔的规定（《出埃及记》12:46、《民数记》9:12：羊羔的骨头一根也不可折断），也有人认为是《诗篇》34:20。
cmp.en: Generally taken as quoting the Old Testament rule for the Passover lamb (Exodus 12:46; Numbers 9:12: none of its bones is to be broken); some point instead to Psalm 34:20.

verses.en: And again another scripture says, “They will look on him whom they pierced.”

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《撒迦利亚书》12:10。
cmp.en: Quoted from Zechariah 12:10.

verses.en: Now after these things Joseph of Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus, but a secret one for fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus; and Pilate gave permission. So he came and took away his body.
And Nicodemus also came, who had first come to him by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
So they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the burial custom of the Jews.
Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
So there, because of the Jewish day of Preparation, since the tomb was near, they laid Jesus.

chapters.title: Chapter 20 · The Empty Tomb; Mary, the Disciples, and Thomas
chapters.intro: Early on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene finds the stone moved from the tomb and runs to tell Peter and the disciple whom Jesus loved; the two run there and find only the linen cloths. Mary stays outside weeping, and Jesus appears to her. That evening he comes to the disciples behind shut doors; Thomas, who was absent, refuses to believe, and eight days later Jesus comes again and shows him his hands and side. The last two verses state why the book was written.

verses.en: Now on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb early, while it was still dark, and sees the stone taken away from the tomb.
So she runs and comes to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and says to them, “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him.”
So Peter and the other disciple went out, and they were going to the tomb.
And the two were running together; and the other disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and came to the tomb first,
and stooping to look in, he sees the linen cloths lying there; yet he did not go in.
So Simon Peter also comes, following him, and went into the tomb; and he sees the linen cloths lying there,
and the face cloth, which had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths but rolled up in a place by itself.
So then the other disciple, who had come to the tomb first, also went in, and he saw and believed;
for as yet they did not understand the scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
So the disciples went away again to their own homes.
But Mary was standing outside at the tomb, weeping. So as she wept, she stooped to look into the tomb,
and she sees two angels in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been lying.
And they say to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She says to them, “They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.”
Having said this, she turned around and sees Jesus standing there, and she did not know that it was Jesus.

Jesus says to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?” Supposing him to be the gardener, she says to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.”
Jesus says to her, “Mary.” She turned and says to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni”—which means Teacher.

cmp.note: 这个词是亚兰话，意思是「我的老师」；经文说的「希伯来话」泛指当时犹太人说的话。后面那句解释是经文原有的（底本放在括号里），不是本站补的，所以白话用破折号隔开。和合本的「夫子」就是老师。
cmp.en: The word is Aramaic, "my teacher"; "Hebrew" in the text is a loose term for the language Jews then spoke. The explanation that follows belongs to the text itself (the edition prints it in parentheses) and is not supplied by this site, so the translations set it off with a dash. The Union Version’s 夫子 (fūzǐ, "master") means teacher.

verses.en: Jesus says to her, “Do not hold on to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father; but go to my brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.’”

cmp.note: 原文是现在时的禁令，通常理解为「不要一直拉着我」；和合本译「不要摸我」。
cmp.en: The Greek is a present-tense prohibition, usually understood as "stop clinging to me"; the Union Version has 不要摸我 (búyào mō wǒ, "do not touch me").

verses.en: Mary Magdalene comes, announcing to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord,” and that he had said these things to her.

So when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and says to them, “Peace to you.”
And having said this, he showed them his hands and his side. So the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
So Jesus said to them again, “Peace to you; just as the Father has sent me, I also send you.”
And having said this, he breathed on them and says to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain the sins of any, they are retained.”
Now Thomas, one of the twelve, the one called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.

So the other disciples were saying to him, “We have seen the Lord.” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the mark of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will certainly not believe.”
And after eight days his disciples were again inside, and Thomas with them. Jesus comes, the doors having been shut, and stood in the midst and said, “Peace to you.”
Then he says to Thomas, “Bring your finger here and see my hands, and bring your hand and put it into my side; and do not be unbelieving, but believing.”
Thomas answered and said to him, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus says to him, “Because you have seen me, have you believed? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
Now Jesus did many other signs in the presence of the disciples, which are not written in this book;
but these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.

chapters.title: Chapter 21 · Breakfast by the Sea; Peter; the Disciple Jesus Loved
chapters.intro: The end of the previous chapter already reads like the close of the book; this chapter continues after it. Jesus shows himself to seven disciples by the Sea of Tiberias: after a night of catching nothing they cast the net where he tells them and take a hundred and fifty-three large fish, and then eat breakfast with him. Three times Jesus asks Peter, "Do you love me?" and tells him to tend his sheep; then the talk turns to the disciple whom Jesus loved. The last two verses close the book a second time.

verses.en: After these things Jesus showed himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias; and he showed himself in this way.
Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.
Simon Peter says to them, “I am going fishing.” They say to him, “We are coming with you too.” They went out and got into the boat, and during that night they caught nothing.
Now when early morning had already come, Jesus stood on the shore; yet the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
So Jesus says to them, “Children, you do not have any fish to eat, do you?” They answered him, “No.”
And he said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it, and they were no longer able to haul it in because of the great number of fish.

So that disciple whom Jesus loved says to Peter, “It is the Lord.” So Simon Peter, hearing that it was the Lord, tied his outer garment around him, for he was stripped for work, and threw himself into the sea;

cmp.note: 原文 gymnos 可以指一丝不挂，也可以指只穿贴身的衣服；这里说的是打鱼干活时的样子。
cmp.en: Greek gymnos can mean naked or wearing only an undergarment; here it describes how he was dressed for fishing.

verses.en: but the other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from the land, only about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of fish.
So when they got out on the land, they see a charcoal fire laid there, and fish lying on it, and bread.
Jesus says to them, “Bring some of the fish that you have just caught.”
So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net to land, full of large fish, a hundred and fifty-three; and although there were so many, the net was not torn.
Jesus says to them, “Come, have breakfast.” Now none of the disciples dared to ask him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord.
Jesus comes and takes the bread and gives it to them, and the fish likewise.
This was now the third time that Jesus was shown to the disciples after he was raised from the dead.

So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?” He says to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” He says to him, “Feed my lambs.”

cmp.note: 这段对话里「爱」原文用了两个动词：耶稣前两次问用 agapaō，彼得三次回答都用 phileō，耶稣第三次问也改用 phileō。这两个词在这卷书里常常通用，这里有没有意思上的分别，看法不一。白话、英文和和合本都只写一个「爱」字。「比这些更深」的「这些」指什么（别的门徒，还是渔船和网），原文也没有说明。
cmp.en: In this exchange the Greek uses two verbs for "love": Jesus asks with agapaō the first two times, Peter answers with phileō all three times, and Jesus’s third question switches to phileō. The two are often used interchangeably in this Gospel, and whether a difference is meant here is disputed. The Chinese versions and the English all write one word. What "these" refers to in "more than these" (the other disciples, or the boats and nets) the text does not say either.

verses.en: He says to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He says to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” He says to him, “Shepherd my sheep.”

He says to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because he said to him the third time, “Do you love me?” and he said to him, “Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you.” Jesus says to him, “Feed my sheep.

Truly, truly, I say to you, when you were younger, you used to gird yourself and walk where you wished; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and carry you where you do not wish to go.”
Now this he said, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. And having said this, he says to him, “Follow me.”
Peter, turning around, sees the disciple whom Jesus loved following, the one who also had leaned back on his chest at the supper and said, “Lord, who is it that is handing you over?”
So Peter, seeing him, says to Jesus, “Lord, and what about this man?”
Jesus says to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”
So this saying went out among the brothers, that that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”
This is the disciple who is testifying about these things and who wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
Now there are also many other things that Jesus did, which if they were written one by one, I suppose that not even the world itself would hold the books that would be written.

title: The Gospel according to John
summary: The fourth Gospel, and the one most unlike the other three: fewer stories and long conversations, in which Jesus, whom Christians hold to be the deliverer sent by God, speaks of who he is and how he is related to the Father, from the opening poem about the Word to his death and resurrection. 21 chapters.

primer.a: 基督教圣经的新约开头有四卷「福音书」，各自把耶稣的事讲了一遍，《约翰福音》是第四卷，也和前三卷最不一样：前三卷讲过的事这里大多没有，这里的事前三卷也大多没有；故事少，长篇的对话和讲话多。一般认为它是四卷里最晚写成的，大约在公元 90 到 100 年前后，用的是当时通行的希腊文。书里没有写作者的名字，只说是「耶稣所爱的那个门徒」作的见证；传统上说这个门徒是约翰，耶稣十二个门徒之一。
全书是一个讲故事的人在叙述，他常常停下来替读者解释一句（「拉比翻出来就是老师」「犹太人和撒玛利亚人不来往」），这些解释是原文就有的。引号里的话是故事里的人说的，其中耶稣的话特别长：他讲自己是谁、从哪里来、和上帝是什么关系。耶稣称上帝为「父」，称自己为「子」；叙述里的「他」，大多数时候指耶稣。
故事发生在大约公元 30 年前后，地点是地中海东岸的犹太人地区（今天的以色列、巴勒斯坦一带），当时归罗马帝国管。犹太人只拜一位上帝，照着祖先摩西传下来的律法过日子，一年里有几个大节期要上耶路撒冷的圣殿去：这卷书的故事就是跟着这些节期走的，耶稣几次上耶路撒冷。很多人在盼望上帝派一位救主来，这位救主希伯来话叫「弥赛亚」，希腊话叫「基督」。

primer.q: 读的时候会卡住的地方
primer.a: 一是开头十八节像一首诗，讲「道」「光」「生命」，很抽象；读不进去可以先从第 1 章第 19 节读起，回头再看。二是耶稣的话里常有一层字面、一层别的意思（重生、活水、粮、光、葡萄树），听的人常常只听懂字面，他再往下讲；书里并不都解释。三是很多话翻来覆去地说，同一个词一章里出现十几次，原文就是这样。四是书里常说「犹太人」怎样怎样：耶稣和门徒自己也都是犹太人，这个词在这卷书里很多时候指的是耶路撒冷那些反对他的人和首领，本站照原文写「犹太人」，没有改。五是有一段（第 7 章第 53 节到第 8 章第 11 节，行淫被捉的妇人）最早的抄本没有，本站照底本译出并在那里写明。
这些词在书里反复出现，先认一下。
terms: 道
原文是「话」「言语」的意思。书的开头用它称呼那位后来成为人的耶稣。
父、子
耶稣称上帝为「父」，称自己为「子」。
永生
永远的生命。书里说它不只是死后的事，信的人现在就有。
世界
有时指上帝所造、所爱的全人类，有时指不认识上帝、与他作对的那一面，要看上下文。
光、黑暗
书里用「光」说上帝和耶稣带来的东西，用「黑暗」说与之相反的一面。
神迹
原文是「记号」。这卷书把耶稣做的奇事叫作记号：意思是它们指向他是谁。
荣耀
上帝的光辉和尊贵。书里常说耶稣「得荣耀」，多半指他被钉十字架和复活那件事。
信
相信、信靠。书里几乎不用名词「信心」，总是用动词。
帮助者
耶稣说他离开以后，父要另派一位来和门徒同在，书里说就是圣灵。和合本译「保惠师」。
犹太人
见上一条「读的时候会卡住的地方」第四点。

primer.a: 全书 21 章。顺着读的话：第 1 章是序诗和最早的几个门徒；第 2–12 章讲耶稣做的七件神迹和围绕它们的长篇对话；第 13–17 章是最后那顿晚饭上，他对门徒说的话和一篇祷告；第 18–21 章是被捕、钉十字架、复活。只想先读一段的话，读第 9 章（一个生来瞎眼的人被治好之后的一连串问话），或者第 11 章（拉撒路）。

primerEn.q: What kind of book this is
primerEn.a: The New Testament of the Christian Bible opens with four "Gospels," each telling the story of Jesus. John is the fourth and the most unlike the others: most of what the first three tell is absent here, and most of what is here is absent from them; there are fewer stories and many long conversations and speeches. It is generally thought to be the latest of the four, written around 90 to 100 CE in the common Greek of the time. The book does not name its author; it says only that it rests on the testimony of "the disciple whom Jesus loved." By tradition that disciple was John, one of the twelve.

A narrator tells the whole story, and often pauses to explain something to the reader ("Rabbi, which translated means Teacher"; "Jews have no dealings with Samaritans"). Those explanations are part of the original. Words in quotation marks are spoken by people in the story, and Jesus’s speeches are especially long: he talks about who he is, where he comes from, and how he is related to God. Jesus calls God "the Father" and himself "the Son." "He" in the narration is usually Jesus.

The story takes place around 30 CE in the Jewish lands on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean (today’s Israel and Palestine), then under the Roman Empire. Jews worshiped one God and lived by the law handed down from their ancestor Moses, and several times a year went up to the temple in Jerusalem for the great festivals. This book’s story follows those festivals, with Jesus going up to Jerusalem several times. Many were waiting for God to send a deliverer, called "Messiah" in Hebrew and "Christ" in Greek.

First, the opening eighteen verses read like a poem about "the Word," "light" and "life," and are very abstract; if they do not go in, start at 1:19 and come back. Second, Jesus’s words often carry a plain sense and another sense (being born again, living water, bread, light, the vine); his hearers usually catch only the plain one and he goes on from there. The book does not always explain. Third, much is said over and over, with the same word a dozen times in a chapter; the original is like that. Fourth, the book often says "the Jews" did this or that. Jesus and his disciples were Jews too; in this book the phrase very often means the people and leaders in Jerusalem who opposed him. This site translates it as it stands. Fifth, one passage (7:53–8:11, the woman caught in adultery) is missing from the earliest manuscripts; this site translates it as its edition prints it and says so there.
These words recur throughout the book.
terms: The Word
Greek logos, "word" or "speech." The opening of the book uses it for the one who later became human as Jesus.
Father, Son
Jesus calls God "the Father" and himself "the Son."
Eternal life
Life that lasts forever. The book says it is not only for after death: those who believe have it now.
The world
Sometimes all humanity, made and loved by God; sometimes the side of it that does not know God and resists him. The context decides.
Light, darkness
The book uses "light" for what God and Jesus bring and "darkness" for its opposite.
Signs
This book’s word for the wonders Jesus does: they point to who he is.
Glory
The splendor and honor of God. When the book says Jesus is "glorified," it mostly means his crucifixion and resurrection.
Believe
To trust. The book almost never uses the noun "faith," always the verb.
Helper
Jesus says that after he leaves, the Father will send another to be with the disciples; the book says this is the Holy Spirit.
The Jews
See the fourth point under "Where you may get stuck."

primerEn.a: The book has 21 chapters. Read straight through: chapter 1 is the opening poem and the first disciples; chapters 2–12 tell seven signs Jesus does and the long conversations around them; chapters 13–17 are what he says to his disciples at their last supper, ending in a prayer; chapters 18–21 are the arrest, crucifixion and resurrection. If you want just one stretch, read chapter 9 (the questioning that follows the healing of a man born blind) or chapter 11 (Lazarus).

compare: 希腊文原文用 SBL Greek New Testament（SBLGNT），只去掉了底本里的校勘符号，经文本身没有动；罗马转写是本站按通行规则机械生成的，不标重音。底本里用双方括号 ⟦ ⟧ 括起来的（7:53–8:11），是编者认为后来才加进这卷书的文字。
白话是写给完全没接触过圣经的人看的：用平常说话的词，把谁在对谁说写清楚。原文没有、但不补就看不懂的字，一律放在圆括号（）里；括号里是通行的解释，不是经文本身。英文版贴着字面译，不加括号，两版对着看就知道哪些是补的。白话、英文和所有说明都是 AI 从希腊文译写的，没有经过圣经学者或教会审阅。
对照栏是 1919 年出版的官话和合译本（和合本），录文取自维基文库，繁体转成简体，几个异体字改成了通行写法，原书的旧式标点照录。维基文库录的是称「神」的版本；本站的白话写「上帝」。人名、地名跟和合本走，只有几处用了今天更常见的写法：约旦河、撒旦、凯撒；和合本的「夫子」本站写「老师」，「保惠师」写「帮助者」。
和合本当年依据的希腊文底本和 SBLGNT 不完全一样，所以有的地方三栏对不上，不是译错。第 5 章第 4 节底本没有、和合本印成小字注，本站留着节号，原文栏放一个「—」。第 7 章第 53 节和合本没有单独编号，那一句在它的第 8 章第 1 节开头，所以这一节的和合本栏是空的。这些地方都在那一节下面写明。
这卷书的希腊文用词很少、句子很短，同一个词反复出现（信、知道、看见、世界、住在……里面）。白话和英文都尽量一个词一种译法，原文重复的地方照样重复，没有为了文字变化换说法。原文里叙述者替读者加的解释（如「翻出来就是……」），是经文本身的话，没有放进圆括号。
compareEn: The Greek is the SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT) with its text-critical sigla removed and nothing else changed; the romanization is generated mechanically by this site under the usual conventions, without accents. Text in double square brackets ⟦ ⟧ (7:53–8:11) is what the editors judge to be a later addition to this Gospel.

The Chinese is written for readers who have never opened a Bible: everyday words, with who is speaking to whom made explicit. Words that are not in the Greek but are needed to follow it are put in parentheses; they give the usual explanation and are not part of the text. The English stays close to the wording and adds no parentheses, so reading the two side by side shows what was supplied. The Chinese, the English and all the notes were translated and written by AI from the Greek and have not been reviewed by biblical scholars or by any church.

The older Chinese version shown alongside is the Mandarin Union Version of 1919, taken from Chinese Wikisource, converted to simplified characters with a few variant characters normalized and its original punctuation kept. Wikisource carries the edition that calls God 神 (Shén); this site’s plain Chinese writes 上帝 (Shàngdì). Names follow the Union Version, except for a few now more commonly written another way: the Jordan, Satan and Caesar.

The Union Version was made from a Greek text that differs in places from SBLGNT, so where the columns disagree it is not always a mistranslation. Verse 5:4 is a small-print note in the Union Version and absent from this edition; the verse number is kept, with a dash in the Greek column. Verse 7:53 has no number of its own in the Union Version, which puts that sentence at the start of 8:1, so nothing is shown beside it. Each such place is explained under that verse.

This Gospel’s Greek uses few words and short sentences, with the same words returning again and again (believe, know, see, world, abide in). Both translations try to keep one rendering per word and to repeat where the Greek repeats, rather than varying for style. The narrator’s own explanations to the reader ("which translated means…") are part of the text and are not put in parentheses.
